items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: Martha Glaser is mentioned by the Interviewer as the source of an anecdote about Erroll Garner; the Interviewee (Charles Mingus) does not mention Martha Glaser or indicate any personal interaction with her.

ctx.x: Blind Tom, he say he can go to Europe A Symphony for him, and and play his own band (unintelligible) he can sit down and play at home. That's pretty good. I couldn't do that. That's (unintelligible) a whole lot of memory in it.

Well, yeah, Erroll Garner -- Martha Glaser told me he went to a concert in Carnegie Hall and went back upstairs, and his studio is upstairs, in Carnegie Hall (inaudible) upstairs, and sat down and played a whole piece through, because he remembered it. But that's how he learned, he couldn't read, he couldn't --
* 19th-Century pianist, born a slave, blind from birth, Viz: Eileen Southern, The Music of Black Americans; Langston Hughes, Black Magic.
